text.tspan: 05 | Dynamic - Ari reserves the final seat; mail is unavailable
One continuous numbered runtime story using the components in 03-components. Read panels A, B, C, D from top to bottom.
PRECONDITION: W17 "Build a tiny game"; owner S10; published; capacity 3; reservations {S21, S22}.
Ari = S23, ari@example.invalid; signed-in cookie is valid; no S23 reservation. Storage works; nobody else acts.
R-W17-S23 below denotes the newly generated reservation ID; t = its creation timestamp.
A | Authenticate and enter Reservation Rules (in-process calls except HTTPS)
B | Decide and persist under one workshop lock (Reservation Rules, Workshop Store, Board Database)
6. BEGIN READ COMMITTED; SELECT W17 FOR UPDATE [SQL/TCP]
8. SELECT reservation WHERE workshop=W17 AND student=S23
10. SELECT COUNT(*) for W17 (later SQL statement)
11. count=2; Rules callback uses this result to check 2 < 3
12. INSERT (R-W17-S23, W17, S23, Ari, ari@example.invalid, t)
14. COMMIT acknowledged; lock released (seat is durable)
C | Request confirmation once after commit; report success even though mail fails
19. Unavailable; no retry and no database change
D | Return the saved reservation and render Ari's success message
21. HTTP 201 + HTML: reservation saved; email unavailable
ARI SEES: Your place in "Build a tiny game" is reserved. Confirmation email is unavailable. Your reservation is still saved.
AFTER: reservations {S21, S22, S23}; W17 unchanged; 0 remaining. A refresh via Board Queries returns the stored S23 seat.
A repeat Reserve returns Existing(R-W17-S23), unchanged, even though full; no additional email request.
University Mail failure changes neither the saved seat nor the success result; no automatic retries.
Legend: each header names a participant and its static type; blue = Board Web App component; green = person/database; grey = external system.
Solid arrow = numbered call; dashed arrow = numbered result or vertical lifeline; panels continue one trace. Store SQL calls run for the Rules callback.
